subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning the vehicle structure as a single module with a chassis root and wheel joints, keeping things simple and using safe part/bone APIs to avoid errors, and now sketching out the truck's dimensions.

I'll keep colors minimal and reuse a clockwork kit for armor paneling and glow textures, then set up the rig with wheel joints along the X axis and a turret/gun joint on top, before starting to lay out the chassis frame geometry.

Writing chassis frame code...

Now I'm placing four wheel axles along the length with radius/width for the tires, adding glowing hub rings and fender boxes over each wheel, then starting the lower hull body geometry.

Shaping the cab profile outline...

Setting up a night-camo panelled paint for the hull, then working out the windshield as a thin tilted box aligned to the slope of the roofline, computing its rotation angle from the slope vector so it sits flush against the cab.

Now I'm adding side window boxes for dark glass panels, headlight light bars with white-cyan glow, and a front grille with slats plus a bumper wedge carrying a hazard-stripe texture.

Then I'm planning the roof sensor array—radar dish, antenna rods, light bar, rangefinder—plus cab armor panels, and shaping the rear cargo bed as an armored hull section with a potential turret platform.

For the turret, I'm weighing options: a rail-gun turret with twin barrels could collide with the cab if pointed forward, so I'm raising it higher and positioning the barrel to extend over the cab roof, running from the rear turret base forward past the cab's height.

Setting up the joint hierarchy next: chassis at the base, turret parented to chassis, and gun parented to turret with its own pivot and direction. I'm giving the turret and gun hinge roles while leaving wheels as plain joints without explicit roles since that's optional.

Now I'm detailing the rear bed -- armor plates with neon strips, missile pod boxes with tube cylinders on each side, exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing tips, tail lights, bumper, tow hook, glowing fuel cells along the sides, and underchassis axles and suspension arms. I'm also planning the surface textures, starting with hazard stripes on the bumper and an emblem decal on the door.

I'm placing the hex emblem on each cab door, working out the plane orientation so the texture reads correctly from outside on both sides, then adding a side stencil panel on the bed and a glowing cyan HUD texture on the windshield plane, leaving camo to the paint and neon bars to plain glow colors.

Then I'm thinking through wheel hub spoke textures with a cyan glow, skipping dash and roof radar details to keep it at five total textures, and checking the color budget stays under the 64 flat-color limit. I'm also verifying ground clearance by working out the tire cylinder geometry and how its vertices sit relative to the ground plane.

Writing helper function for boxes...

Setting up the cylinder helper and planning the overall part budget, aiming for around 250 parts using imports from the builder library and material kits.

I'm working out the hull's paint treatment—layering panelled textures over a camo patch base with specific seams and rivet detail—while checking the texel density needed to keep surface seams crisp at this scale.

Given the thinness of the seams relative to texel resolution, I decide to bump paint size to 2048 and restrict the detailed paint to just the cab and bed to keep things lightweight while still readable. Now I'm defining the color palette: dark charcoal, steel, orange accent, cyan, magenta, red, yellow, and a deep glass tint to give it that cyberpunk edge.

Building the truck's skeleton...

Adding wheel tires and considering tread detail, trying to keep part count manageable by simplifying each tire to just two merged cylinders instead of individual tread lugs.

Adding wheel hub plates, fenders over the wheel arches, and a mud flap hanging behind the rear axle...

I'm noticing the bed hull overlaps the wheels in height, so I'm adjusting the hull to sit higher (y=1.3 to 2.0) while keeping the wheels slightly wider on x so they clear under the overhang, leaving just enough gap for the cab bottom profile at 1.05.

I'm raising the cab profile's bottom edge to y=1.3 to avoid conflicting with the front wheel tops, reshaping it into a tall cab-over design with a sloped hood and bumper extending to z=3.5, and I'm now laying out the wheelbase across four axles with the hull running from z=-4.1 to 0.1.

Now I'm adding a belly armor plate beneath the chassis rails, positioned to clear the wheel hubs, and detailing the cab with windshield panels, door seams, handles, and side mirrors with camera lenses mounted near the top corners.

Then I'm designing the front fascia as a flat COE grille with glowing cyan slats, headlights, fog lights, a reinforced ram bumper with brush guard bars, tow hooks, and a winch cylinder across the front, followed by roof details including an armor plate, sensor mast, satellite dish, and a glowing light bar.

Now I'm adding side armor ribs, bed slats, and cargo hatches, then working out missile pod placement so they don't collide with the turret — relocating them to the rear at angled positions with twin tube clusters per pod, rotated outward for an aggressive stance.

Writing the coordinate transform helper...

I'm realizing the gun mount placement conflicts with the cab roof, so I need to raise the turret body and reposition the barrel cradle higher to avoid collision with the hull geometry.

Adding the muzzle brake, recoil spring, and gun joint placement, then checking overall vehicle length fits within the front and rear bumpers. Now I'm working out the rear bumper, tail lights, and exhaust stack placement, making sure they clear the hull and cab geometry.

Placing the exhaust stacks properly with their heat shields, then adding cargo rails, antenna whips at the rear corners, and neon underglow strips along the chassis and hull edges for the cyber aesthetic.

I'm adding stenciled text plates to the hull sides via textured planes, plus spotlights near the cab and glowing battery cell rows along the bottom between the axles.

I'm also roughing out skirt panels beneath the cab with inset battery cells, and lathing a satellite dish shape for a roof-mounted antenna, working through the outline points to keep the profile loop non-self-intersecting.

Writing hazard-stripe SVG texture...

Now I'm sketching the door emblem design—an orange hexagon outline with a triangular visor and "77" text—plus a stencil-style "ARES-77 // HEAVY STRIKE" banner texture.

Designing the HUD overlay with a dark teal backdrop, cyan reticle lines, and glowing text, along with a hub texture showing a dark disc with a cyan ring, orange spokes, and bolts. I'm deciding to skip a separate grille texture and reuse the box geometry instead, then working through how plane parts attach with proper orientation—figuring out the up-vector handling for angled placements like the windshield.

Now I'm adding camo stripes and markings for extra detail, plus small intricate touches like cab ladders, handrails, roof rails, and an ammo belt built from sweep geometry along a curved path. I'm sketching out cable and hose sweeps between the turret and hull using catmull-rom paths, along with thin antenna whips and a spare wheel mounted on the rear of the hull.

I'm skipping the spare tire placement and instead adding jerry cans as small olive boxes positioned along the hull sides between the axles, plus floodlights near the turret. I'm also confirming the Euler rotation order for parts and designing a neon torus ring around the turret rim with a glowing cyan material, oriented to face upward.

Now I'm adding similar glowing torus rings at the wheel hubs, then writing the cab geometry using an extrusion helper that takes an outline profile and sweeps it along an axis with bevel and color, making sure the coordinate axes and glow materials are set up correctly.

I'm checking that the cab outline points form a sensible convex shape, then figuring out the windshield slope angle (about 45 degrees) so I can orient a thin box along that slope for the glass panel.

Now I'm offsetting the windshield box slightly outward from the slab surface along its normal and sizing a HUD plane to fit within the frame, making sure the embedded glass box's outer face sits just above the cab's slanted surface.

Next I'm working out the side window placement, checking that the glass box dimensions and position stay within the cab's half-width and don't cross the roof's slope boundary at the upper edge.

Then I'm adding a door emblem plane and seam lines on the cab side, followed by sketching the hull box dimensions and position, and an upper armored deck layer sitting above it. I'm also revising the turret base height to align with the hull's ring at y=2.3, adjusting the turret profile coordinates to match this new base level.

Still working out dimensions...

Still writing cables and glow strips...
